= Repository rulesets

[IMPORTANT]
====
**GitHub does not read this directory.** Unlike `.github/workflows/`,
`.github/dependabot.yml` or `.github/settings.yml`, ruleset JSON in a repository
path is *not* auto-applied by any GitHub feature. These files are
**documentation of intent plus a ready-to-POST payload** — nothing more.

A ruleset only takes effect once someone applies it via the REST API or imports
it in the web UI. Until then the protection described here **is not in force**.
====

== Applying a ruleset

Per ADR-0003 the *Configure* stage is an operator stage: identity, visibility and
branch/tag protection are set out of band. Automation is future work and must not
be described as existing.

[source,bash]
----
# Apply (create) a ruleset on the current repo:
gh api --method POST \
  -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \
  "/repos/{owner}/{repo}/rulesets" \
  --input .github/rulesets/base.json

# List what is actually in force — the only authoritative answer:
gh api "/repos/{owner}/{repo}/rulesets" --jq '.[] | "\(.id)\t\(.name)\t\(.enforcement)"'

# Update an existing ruleset in place (needs its numeric id from the list above):
gh api --method PUT \
  "/repos/{owner}/{repo}/rulesets/<id>" \
  --input .github/rulesets/base.json
----

== Files

`base.json`:: Canonical branch protection ruleset for the default branch (`~DEFAULT_BRANCH`).
Enforces deleted-branch protection, linear history, squash merge, signatures and required
status checks, without unsatisfiable coverage or deadlocking approval requirements.
Sourced verbatim from `hyperpolymath/standards` `config/rulesets/base.json` (§7.3).

`branch-floor.json`:: The irreducible branch floor for the default branch: deletion and
non-fast-forward protection only, with no bypass actors. This is the ruleset that keeps a
branch recoverable when the richer `Base` ruleset is unavailable or has been removed.
Sourced verbatim from `hyperpolymath/standards` `config/rulesets/branch-floor.json`.

`require-signed-commits.json`:: Standalone, zero-bypass `required_signatures` on the default
branch (D215). Every new repo is born with it. See `hyperpolymath/standards`
`docs/SIGNING-POLICY.adoc`. Sourced verbatim from `config/rulesets/require-signed-commits.json`.

`require-linear-history.json`:: Standalone, zero-bypass `required_linear_history` (D216).
Pair it with squash-only merge settings. A new repo starts with no merge commits, so it is
always linear-safe. Sourced verbatim from `config/rulesets/require-linear-history.json`.

`Immutable-Tags.json`:: Makes release tags immutable — blocks tag deletion,
non-fast-forward updates, and overwrites, and requires signed tags.

[NOTE]
====
Files here are named to match the *live ruleset name*, which is not always the
upstream filename. Upstream ships `branch-floor.json` and `immutable-tags.json`
(lowercase, with a matching lowercase `name` inside the JSON); this repository's
`Immutable-Tags.json` declares `"name": "Immutable-Tags"`. Renaming a file here
changes nothing on GitHub, but it does change which upstream file it is diffed
against — keep that in mind when syncing.
====

== What is actually enforced on this repository

Files are intent; this table is fact. Regenerate it with:

[source,bash]
----
gh api "/repos/{owner}/{repo}/rulesets" --jq '.[] | "\(.id)\t\(.name)\t\(.enforcement)\t\(.target)"'
----

|===
| Live ruleset | Enforcement | Target | Rules reported by the API

| `Require-Linear-History` (`24258228`) | active | branch | `required_linear_history`
| `Secret-Scan-Floor` (`24309812`) | active | branch | *none* — `rules: []`
| `Immutable-Tags` (`22959911`) | active | tag | creation, deletion, non-fast-forward, update, required signatures
|===

[IMPORTANT]
====
Measured 2026-11-08. Two corrections against the previous version of this table:

. `Base` (`23218684`) no longer exists. `GET /rulesets/23218684` returns
*404 Not Found*, and the repository's ruleset list does not include it. Every
claim in the drift notes below about what `Base` enforces — code scanning,
Copilot review, `deletion`, `non_fast_forward` — describes a ruleset that is
gone. `GET /rules/branches/main` now returns exactly one rule
(`required_linear_history`, from `24258228`).
. `Secret-Scan-Floor` (`24309812`) is `active` on `target: branch` with
`conditions.ref_name.include: ["~DEFAULT_BRANCH"]`, but it carries **zero
rules**. It therefore requires *no* status check. `scan / gitleaks` is
*produced* by `.github/workflows/secret-scanner.yml`, not required by anything.

So as of 2026-11-08 `main` is protected only by `required_linear_history`.
This is a record of the live state, not an endorsement: a status-check floor
that enforces nothing is not a floor. Restoring it is an owner action on the
live ruleset and a deliberate decision about which contexts to require, not
something these files can do on their own — `base.json` is upstream-sourced and
its `required_status_checks` is deliberately empty.
====

=== Known drift between these files and what is live

The files below are *not* a transcript of the live rulesets. This is the
divergence as of 2026-10-25, recorded rather than silently reconciled because
`base.json` is sourced verbatim from upstream and must not be forked here.

*Live rulesets that no synced file describes* ::

CORRECTED 2026-11-08: the previous text here stated that `code_scanning` (CodeQL
and Hypatia) and `copilot_code_review` are "enforced live in `Base`
(`23218684`)", and that `Secret-Scan-Floor` (`24309812`) "enforces
`required_status_checks` for `scan / gitleaks`". Both statements are now false.
`Base` returns 404 and is absent from the ruleset list; `Secret-Scan-Floor` is
active but has `rules: []`. No live branch ruleset carries a `code_scanning`
rule either, so CodeQL and Hypatia currently *report* results without gating
merges. What remains true is the file-vs-live gap: upstream's nearest
equivalent for code scanning,
`config/rulesets/Optimus-Extras.json`, declares `code_scanning` with an *empty*
`code_scanning_tools` list, so it would not describe a populated live rule
either. Conversely, `branch-floor.json` is retained here as the irreducible
recovery payload even though `Branch-Floor` is not mounted as a live ruleset and
nothing currently supplies its `deletion` / `non_fast_forward` coverage.

*Removed from live `Base` on 2026-10-02 (owner decision)* ::

NOTE (2026-11-08): the history below is retained, but `Base` was subsequently
deleted outright — the ruleset returns 404 and is absent from the ruleset list.
Every rule discussed here is now unenforced, including the `deletion` and
`non_fast_forward` coverage noted further down.

`Scorecard` was dropped from `code_scanning_tools`, and the `code_coverage` rule
(minimum 80%, max drop 5) was deleted. Neither could ever be satisfied by a pull
request. `scorecard.yml` runs only on `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch`, and
Scorecard scores repository posture rather than a diff, so with
`alerts_threshold: all` any standing finding would have blocked every PR. Nothing
in this template produces a coverage report: `rust-ci / llvm-cov` is skipped
because the template has no Rust. The result was that every PR sat `BLOCKED` until
an admin bypass (#219). CodeQL and Hypatia both upload results on pull requests,
so they stay. Do not add either rule back without a producer that runs on
`pull_request`.

*`base.json` rules that are not in force* ::

`required_linear_history` is in `base.json` but not in live `Base`; it is
enforced by the separate `Require-Linear-History` ruleset. `required_status_checks` (an empty list, so a no-op) and the
`pull_request` rule are likewise absent from live `Base`. (`non_fast_forward` was
live in `Base` as of 2026-10-02; `branch-floor.json` also specifies it as a
retained recovery payload, though `Branch-Floor` is not mounted as a separate live ruleset. With `Base` deleted as of 2026-11-08, no live ruleset supplies `non_fast_forward` or `deletion` on branches.)

*`Immutable-Tags.json` lags the live ruleset* ::

The live tag ruleset includes a `creation` rule; this file does not. Upstream
`immutable-tags.json` also populates `bypass_actors` (repository-role 5 and an
integration) with `bypass_mode: always`, and this file declares none.

[WARNING]
====
`bypass_actors` cannot be diffed from a low-privilege token: the REST API returns
`null` for that field unless the caller has admin on the repository. Absence of
`bypass_actors` in the output above is *not* evidence that none are configured.
====

== Verifying

Do not infer that a ruleset is active because the JSON is present. Check with the
`gh api ... /rulesets` list above. A ruleset that exists as a file but was never
POSTed is the protection equivalent of a check that cannot fail.

Conversely, do not infer that the estate is protected because a ruleset exists.
A ruleset with `enforcement: disabled` is inert, and a `pull_request` rule with
`allowed_merge_methods: []` can never be satisfied at all.
